producer_report.summary:
I added docs/design/reviews/squash-chain-landing-review-1.md. It is an independent review of the squash-chain landing design, in the format of the existing reviews, and no code, config or records changed. Its verdict is approve with changes, with 3 major, 5 minor and 2 nit findings. Each finding has a severity, evidence from the design section and the code or decisions it rests on, and a recommended change. The review also has a table checking the design's claims against `invariant.rs`, `jobs.rs`, `history.rs`, `records.rs`, `attrs.rs` and D60 and D66–D69. It lists nine failure modes that `landing_tests.rs` does not cover.

The main findings:
- **R1-M1:** the chain-ordering rule breaks when fingerprints repeat, for example when one job reverts another or changes no governed content.
- **R1-M2:** the claim that the final verifier saw the whole tree is not supported. The v0 design says the verifier gets only a diff and stat of its own candidate.
- **R1-M3:** fingerprints computed under different path-classification rules may not link.
- **R1-m1:** `jobs::check` also needs to change, because it calls `landing_job` and requires a single job per commit. The design's follow-up list leaves it out.

`cargo test --locked` passes, and `git status` shows only the one new untracked file.

I did not run `cargo fmt` or clippy. I also did not open `docs/enforcement.md` or `docs/architecture.md` to check the pointers the design claims in §6. All findings come from reading the code; I did not run the proposed rule."

checks_run.note: All suites passed, including xtask policy tests (wording scan) with the new file present.

open_issues: Findings R1-M1, R1-M3 and the 'untested failure modes' are reasoned from reading; none was reproduced by running code.
The design's pointers in docs/enforcement.md and docs/architecture.md were not verified.
mistakes: Did not run cargo fmt/clippy; only a docs file was added.
Read landing_tests.rs only to line 470; the test list comes from a grep of #[test] and the read portion.
Did not open docs/enforcement.md or docs/architecture.md to check the pointers the design claims in §6; the review says so.
learnings: jobs::check (jobs.rs ~330-344) also calls landing_job and requires a single job per commit, a second caller the design's follow-up list omits.
The v0 design (§6.3) says the verifier gets only a CandidateView (diff and stat), which undercuts the 'verifier saw the whole tree' claim.
xtask/tests/policy.rs scans docs for banned words, so review text must avoid them.
landing_tests.rs holds six tests, all single-job.
desires: A way to run the proposed chain rule against a hand-built two-job commit, to turn the inferred findings into measured ones.
